{{BLP sources|date=July 2022}}{{Family name hatnote|[[Xie (surname)|Xie]]|lang=Chinese}}

'''Xie Shengwu''' ({{zh|s=谢绳武}}; born November 22, 1943)  is a Chinese [[physicist]] who served as President of [[Shanghai Jiao Tong University]] from 1997 to 2006.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://english.people.com.cn/200607/17/eng20060717_283786.html|title=Chinese academics call for gov't support in research use|date=17 July 2006|work=[[People's Daily]]|access-date=2019-11-23}}</ref>

Xie was born in [[Shaoxing]], [[Zhejiang Province]]. From 1960 to 1966, he studied in the department of engineering physics at SJTU, majoring in nuclear reactors. From 1966 to 1970, he was a teaching assistant in the physics teaching office at SJTU. Xie later became a teaching assistant and vice director of the laser research lab. From 1978 to 1981, he studied optics in the department of applied physics at SJTU and obtained a master's degree. From 1981 to 1991, Xie was elevated to a full professor of physics, and later served as the chair of the physics department. From 1991, he served as the vice president of SJTU and a member of the University's CPC standing committee. He became the dean of the graduate school and a doctor's supervisor in 1994.

From July 1997, Xie served as the president of SJTU until his retirement on November 27, 2006.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.shanghai.gov.cn/shanghai/node17256/node18151/userobject22ai23456.html|title=New uni president|date=28 November 2006|publisher=www.shanghai.gov.cn|access-date=2010-12-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110718222745/http://www.shanghai.gov.cn/shanghai/node17256/node18151/userobject22ai23456.html|archive-date=2011-07-18|url-status=dead}}</ref>
